summary.text: Kwame Raoul is the Democratic Attorney General of Illinois and is seeking a third term. A former Cook County prosecutor and state senator from 2004 to 2019, he has filed or joined numerous lawsuits against Trump administration actions on funding, tariffs and immigration enforcement.

paragraphs.text: Raoul was born in Chicago to Haitian immigrants.
He earned a bachelor's degree from DePaul University in 1987 and a law degree from Chicago-Kent College of Law.
He began his career as a senior staff attorney for the City Colleges of Chicago and then worked as a prosecutor in the Cook County State's Attorney's Office.
He was a partner at Quarles & Brady LLP and at a second national corporate law firm.
Raoul served in the Illinois State Senate, representing the 13th District, from 2004 to 2019, a total of 14 years.
He was initially appointed to the seat that opened when Barack Obama was elected to the U.S. Senate.
Raoul was first elected attorney general in 2018 and was sworn in as Illinois' 42nd Attorney General in 2019.
He began a second term on January 9, 2023.
In his current term the Sun-Times reports that he has joined lawsuits over the Trump administration's tariffs, cuts to public health grants and access to mail-in ballots, among other issues.
